source.citation: US FDA Drug Safety Communication: FDA revises warnings regarding use of the diabetes medicine metformin in certain patients with reduced kidney function (2016-04-08)
source.note: Paraphrased by project; reference only until reviewed.

text: Metformin and kidney function (US FDA): contraindicated if eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2; starting metformin at eGFR 30-45 is not recommended; if eGFR falls below 45 in a patient already taking it, assess benefits and risks of continuing; stop if eGFR falls below 30; check eGFR at least annually.

source.citation: Merck Manual Professional Version: Hypertensive Emergencies (M. R. Weir; full review Feb 2025)
source.note: Paraphrased by project; reference only until reviewed.

text: Severe hypertension (generally SBP >= 180 and/or DBP >= 120 mm Hg) with signs of acute target-organ damage (e.g., chest pain, dyspnoea, neurological deficit, confusion, visual loss) is a hypertensive emergency needing immediate care; severe elevation without target-organ damage (urgency) does not require immediate lowering and is managed with oral therapy and follow-up.
